title: Effects of alcohol on emotion recognition: An alcohol-administration trial.
journal: Psychology of addictive behaviors : journal of the Society of Psychologists in Addictive Behaviors
abstract: Alcohol consumption influences emotion recognition accuracy, with notable sex differences observed in its effects on social behavior.

title: Alcohol in the Workplace: A Qualitative Study of Employees' Experiences With Employer-Supported Alcohol Treatment
abstract: Explores employees' experiences with employer-supported alcohol treatment in Sweden, highlighting its impact on health and work performance.

title: Alcohol Expectancies, Emotional States, and Alcohol-Related Consequences among Junior College Students in China: A Full Mediation Model of Alcohol Consumption
abstract: Examines the interplay between emotional states, alcohol expectancies, and alcohol-related consequences among Chinese junior college students.

title: Impact of alcohol exclusion law repeal on inpatient alcohol-related diagnoses
journal: The International journal on drug policy
abstract: Investigates the effect of alcohol exclusion law repeal on the documentation of inpatient alcohol-related diagnoses in the US.

title: Alcohol Cues Invigorate Aversion-Resistant Alcohol Drinking
abstract: Explores how alcohol-related cues exacerbate aversion-resistant drinking, a hallmark of alcohol use disorder.

title: Adolescent Exposure to Nicotine and Ethanol Attenuates Adult Nicotine Reward Sensitivity in Rats
abstract: Exposure to nicotine and alcohol during adolescence can alter the brain's reward system, reducing sensitivity to nicotine's pleasurable effects in adulthood.

title: Effects of E-Liquid Formulations on Nicotine Vapor Pressure and Implications for Nicotine Delivery and Toxicity
abstract: Different e-liquid formulations affect how nicotine is delivered and absorbed, influencing its potency and potential health risks.

title: Evaluating cannabis-nicotine substitution and demand during nicotine cessation treatment in young adults: protocol for a prospective, remote 12-week nicotine cessation trial in the USA
abstract: This study explores how cannabis use affects nicotine cessation in young adults, focusing on patterns of dual substance use.

title: The Case for a Pregnancy-Specific Nicotine Policy
abstract: This paper argues for stricter policies on nicotine use during pregnancy due to its harmful effects on fetal development.

title: Total and unprotonated (freebase) nicotine content in new types of oral 'tobacco-free' nicotine products
abstract: Emerging tobacco-free nicotine products vary widely in nicotine content and pH, raising concerns about their safety and regulation.

title: Early life nicotine vapor exposure increases nicotine vapor seeking in adult male rats
abstract: Exposure to nicotine vapor during adolescence increases the likelihood of seeking nicotine later in adulthood.

title: Guideline No. 470: Nicotine and Pregnancy
journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
abstract: This guideline provides recommendations for managing nicotine use during pregnancy, emphasizing cessation and harm reduction.

title: A metabolon channels nicotine biosynthesis
abstract: Researchers uncover the complex biochemical pathway that plants use to produce nicotine, revealing new enzymes and intermediates.

title: Development of a model to predict nicotine pharmacokinetics from oral nicotine pouches
abstract: A new model predicts how nicotine is absorbed from oral nicotine pouches, aiding regulatory approval and safety assessments.

title: Price comparisons for the leading brands of oral nicotine pouches and cigarettes
abstract: This study compares the cost of nicotine pouches to cigarettes, highlighting affordability as a factor in their growing popularity.

title: Nicotine Effects on Vestibular Function in Pilot Selection
abstract: Nicotine's impact on spatial orientation and vestibular function is evaluated in the context of pilot selection.

title: Psilocybin-induced behavioral and cellular effects
abstract: Psilocybin affects the nucleus accumbens, a brain region involved in reward and emotion, suggesting potential therapeutic benefits for psychiatric disorders.

title: Feasibility and Tolerability of Psilocybin for Phantom Limb Pain
abstract: Psilocybin shows promise in alleviating phantom limb pain, a condition resistant to conventional treatments, by modulating brain pathways involved in pain perception.

title: Balancing safety and access in Oregon's psilocybin services
journal: The International journal on drug policy
abstract: Oregon's psilocybin services program provides insights into balancing access to psychedelics with safety measures, offering a model for other jurisdictions.

title: The “dark magic mushroom” co-produces amatoxins and psilocybin
abstract: A rare mushroom species produces both psilocybin and amatoxins, highlighting the complexity of fungal chemistry and the risks of misidentification.

title: Mapping excitatory synaptic plasticity evoked by single-dose psilocybin in mice
abstract: A single dose of psilocybin induces long-lasting changes in synaptic plasticity, potentially explaining its antidepressant effects.

title: Beyond psilocybin: Do magic mushroom preparations contain other compounds with pharmacological effects?
abstract: Psilocybin mushrooms may contain additional compounds that influence their pharmacological effects, suggesting complexity beyond psilocybin alone.

title: From caffeine use motives to sleep disturbance: network and structural equation modeling of caffeine use disorder and depression among caffeine consumers
abstract: This study explores how caffeine use motives, such as staying awake or improving focus, are linked to sleep disturbances and depressive symptoms among university students. It highlights the complex relationship between caffeine consumption and mental health.

title: Effect of Transcutol P on Percutaneous Absorption of Gel Containing Pure Synthetic Caffeine or Plant-Extracted Natural Caffeine
abstract: This research compares the skin absorption of synthetic and natural caffeine gels, finding that Transcutol P enhances caffeine penetration, which could improve its effectiveness in treating skin conditions like cellulite and hair loss.

title: Caffeine and Headache: Exploring the Multifaceted Relationship
abstract: This review examines caffeine's dual role in headache relief and its potential to trigger headaches, focusing on its effects on adenosine receptors and its use in treating migraines.

title: Caffeine Consumption and Rhinologic Symptom Severity
journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
abstract: This study investigates whether caffeine consumption worsens rhinologic symptoms like nasal congestion and sinus pressure, finding mixed effects depending on individual sensitivity.

title: Neuroprotective potential of caffeine in a rotenone-induced Drosophila model of Parkinsonism.
abstract: This research explores caffeine's potential to protect against Parkinson's disease by reducing neurotoxicity in fruit flies, suggesting a possible role in mitigating neurodegenerative conditions.

title: Impact of Interactions between Melanoidins and Caffeine on the Bitter Taste of Coffee Beverages
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: This study investigates how caffeine interacts with other compounds in coffee to influence its bitter taste, finding that melanoidins play a key role in modulating flavor perception.

title: The Effect of CYP1A2 Gene Polymorphisms on Caffeine Pharmacokinetics and Exercise Performance in Male Recreational Athletes
abstract: This research examines how genetic differences in caffeine metabolism affect its ability to enhance exercise performance, showing that fast metabolizers benefit more from caffeine's stimulant effects.

title: Caffeine and Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
abstract: This statement reviews the evidence on caffeine's effects on cardiovascular health, concluding that moderate consumption is generally safe but may pose risks for individuals with certain heart conditions.

title: Rapid bedside assessment of serum caffeine concentrations using an immunochromatographic screening kit: evaluation of analytical and diagnostic performance in acute caffeine poisoning
abstract: This study evaluates a rapid test kit for detecting caffeine poisoning, showing its effectiveness in emergency settings for identifying potentially lethal caffeine levels.

title: Paper-based electrochemical sensor for direct detection of caffeine in commercial beverage samples
abstract: This research develops a portable, biodegradable sensor for detecting caffeine in beverages, offering a simple and eco-friendly method for caffeine analysis.

title: Mindfulness meditation increases interictal epileptiform discharges in meditation-naïve surgical epilepsy patients
abstract: Novice meditation temporarily increased abnormal brain waves in epilepsy patients, suggesting meditation affects neural excitability differently in sensitive brains.

title: Multiscale cardiorespiratory complexity reveals autonomic signatures of Rajyoga meditation
abstract: Advanced meditators showed unique heart rate patterns suggesting improved nervous system balance during practice.

title: Personalized prediction of response to three meditation practices: A randomized controlled trial
abstract: Different people benefit from different meditation styles - matching practice type to individual traits improved wellbeing outcomes.

title: Defining Advanced Meditation: A Conceptual Foundation for a Comprehensive Contemplative Science beyond Mindfulness Meditation, Basic Meditation, and Other Non-Meditative Consciousness-Altering Practices
abstract: Researchers proposed criteria to distinguish beginner from advanced meditation, including lasting changes in self-awareness and attention control.

title: EEG dynamics during prolonged Samatha meditation: A case study across levels of meditation expertise
abstract: Brain wave patterns differed significantly between novice and expert meditators, with experts showing more stable alpha rhythms linked to focused attention.

title: The Neurodynamic Core of Meditation: Dissociating Meditation from Rest and Task in a Reliability-based EEG study
abstract: Meditation creates a unique brain state distinct from both resting and focused tasks, characterized by balanced frontal and parietal lobe activity.

title: Sources of joy among older African American women: A qualitative analysis
abstract: This study explores how older African American women define, experience, and sustain joy in their everyday lives, highlighting its role in health and well-being.

title: Moments That Matter: Exploring Autistic Adolescents' and Their Families' Joy Through Family Journals
journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
abstract: This qualitative study examines how autistic adolescents and their families experience and co-create joy, providing insights into the role of joy in family life.

title: The impact of virtual reality on curiosity, joy, and engagement
abstract: This study investigates how virtual reality influences curiosity, joy, and engagement, exploring the relationships among these factors in an educational context.

title: Defining joy after a genetic diagnosis: A narrative inquiry
abstract: This study explores how patients and families experience joy after receiving a genetic diagnosis, highlighting positive aspects of the diagnostic journey.

title: Partnering with AI to create joy-centered personalized learning in a post-pandemic world
abstract: This paper discusses how AI can be used to create personalized learning experiences that foster joy and engagement in STEM education.

title: Can joy and compassion buffer against hostility following provocation? An experimental study
abstract: This study examines how joy and compassion can reduce hostility and improve emotional well-being following provocation.

title: Cognition and future depression: associations with risk in those with and without a history of depression
abstract: Cognitive impairments predict both first-onset and recurrent depression, suggesting cognitive screening could help identify at-risk individuals before mood symptoms appear.

title: Interleukin 6 as a Treatment Target for Depression: A Proof-of-Concept Randomized Clinical Trial
abstract: Blocking the inflammatory cytokine IL-6 shows promise for reducing depressive symptoms in treatment-resistant cases, supporting the inflammation-depression link.

title: Stressful life events and depression onset: A longitudinal investigation of depression course subtypes
journal: Journal of psychopathology and clinical science
abstract: Stressful life events trigger different depression trajectories, with some individuals recovering quickly while others develop chronic patterns influenced by early risk factors.

title: Combined effect of metabolic syndrome and cancer on depression
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction and cancer history combine to significantly increase depression risk, highlighting the body-brain connection in mood disorders.

title: Socioeconomic and lifestyle factors predict the association between sleep health and depression
abstract: Poor sleep quality strongly predicts depression, particularly in individuals with lower socioeconomic status, suggesting sleep interventions could help prevent depression.

title: Transition time from manic and mixed episodes to depression: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Bipolar patients frequently transition from manic to depressive phases within weeks, with this pattern potentially representing a distinct subtype requiring specific treatments.

title: Sleep Deprivation, Social Media Addiction, and Associated Factors in Children After Natural Disasters
abstract: This study examines sleep deprivation and social media addiction in children indirectly exposed to earthquakes, revealing significant disruptions in sleep patterns and emotional regulation.

title: Fidelity of remote, video-monitored experimental total sleep deprivation
abstract: This study validates at-home sleep deprivation protocols, showing significant impacts on learning, stress responses, and cognitive performance.

title: Sleep deprivation as a modulator of thyroid function: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: This meta-analysis links sleep deprivation to thyroid dysfunction, highlighting its broader endocrine disruptions beyond just brain function.

title: Sleep deprivation increases levels of the synaptic density marker SV2A in the human brain
abstract: Using PET imaging, this study shows that sleep deprivation disrupts synaptic homeostasis, leading to excessive synaptic potentiation and impaired neural efficiency.

title: Restoring access to long-term social recognition memories disrupted by sleep deprivation
abstract: This study demonstrates that sleep deprivation disrupts social memory consolidation in mice, leading to 'social amnesia' that can be reversed with recovery sleep.

title: Neurophysiology of Sleep-Deprivation Part 1: Effects of Sleep-Deprivation on Event-Related Potentials (ERPs)-Systematic and Mechanistic Review
abstract: This review examines how sleep deprivation alters event-related potentials (ERPs), revealing disruptions in early sensory processing and later cognitive control stages.

title: Beyond Performance: Cognitive Overload and Related Cognitive, Psychophysiological, and Performance States in Competitive Esports-A Scoping Review
abstract: Examines how esports players manage cognitive demands during high-stakes competition, revealing overload patterns similar to traditional athletes.

title: Procrastination and online social anxiety: the mediating role of cognitive overload and the moderating influence of mindfulness
abstract: Shows how digital procrastination creates cognitive overload, which then amplifies social anxiety in online environments.

title: Algorithmic academic framing in AI-driven smart libraries: a moderated mediation model of personalized learning and cognitive overload in academic decision-making
abstract: Investigates how AI educational tools can paradoxically increase cognitive load despite their intention to personalize learning.

title: Mitigating Cognitive Overload in Nursing Education: An Integrative Review
abstract: Identifies strategies to prevent cognitive overload in nursing students balancing academic and clinical demands.

title: Cognitive overload in multimedia language learning: a review of attention limits and instructional design strategies
abstract: Analyzes how multimedia language tools can exceed learners' cognitive capacity without proper design considerations.

title: Deciphering the underlying repercussions of cognitive overload on university students' fatigue, frustration and academic productivity: Implementation of stimulus-organism-response model
abstract: Documents how sustained cognitive overload leads to academic burnout through measurable fatigue and frustration pathways.

title: Community physical activity environments and physical activity levels among older adults: a hierarchical analysis of environmental dimensions
abstract: This study explores how community environments influence physical activity levels in older adults, highlighting the importance of accessible and supportive spaces for active aging.

title: Self-Determined Motivation and Physical Activity in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
abstract: This research examines how intrinsic motivation influences physical activity in COPD patients, emphasizing the role of self-determination in sustaining active behavior.

title: Occupational Physical Activity and Hypertension: A Narrative Review.
abstract: This review summarizes evidence on the relationship between occupational physical activity and hypertension, highlighting inconsistent findings and potential mechanisms.

title: Physical activity levels, perceived barriers, and stages of behaviour change for physical activity among urban university students in Bangladesh
abstract: This study investigates physical activity levels and barriers among university students, emphasizing the impact of urbanization and technology on inactivity.

title: Bridging Healthcare and Community Physical Activity: The Emerging Role of Physical Activity for Health in Ireland
abstract: This paper explores the integration of community-based exercise programs into healthcare systems for chronic disease management and prevention.

title: Mapping the behavioural and motivational network of youth physical activity
abstract: This study maps the behavioral and motivational factors influencing physical activity in youth, highlighting the interconnected nature of these factors.

title: Beyond fear: dual task interventions are effective for fear and non-fear memories
abstract: Shows that trauma memories involve multiple emotions beyond fear, and dual-task interventions (like EMDR) can help process these complex emotional memories.

title: Self-compassion and earthquake fear: the mediating roles of resilience and fear of happiness
abstract: Demonstrates how self-compassion builds resilience against chronic fear by reducing avoidance of positive emotions that often follows trauma.

title: Innate anxiety in rats determines vulnerability to social fear conditioning and social fear memory
abstract: Reveals genetic predisposition influences how social trauma forms lasting fear memories, with high-anxiety individuals showing stronger fear conditioning.

title: Paraventricular thalamus hyperactivity mediates stress-induced sensitization of unlearned fear but not stress-enhanced fear learning (SEFL)
abstract: Identifies a key brain region that amplifies generalized fear after stress, separate from circuits involved in learning specific fear associations.

title: Facing Fear in the Operating Room: A Qualitative Investigation Into the Causes of and Management Strategies for Surgeon Fear in the Operating Room
abstract: Explores how high-stakes professionals experience and regulate acute fear, highlighting cognitive strategies to maintain performance under threat.

title: PMAT enhances sexual dimorphism of fear behaviors and facilitates female mice's generalized contextual fear extinction
abstract: Shows sex differences in fear extinction, with females benefiting more from monoamine transporter modulation during fear memory updating.

title: Sadness, Risk Direction, and Correction of Health Misinformation: Effects on Beliefs and Sharing Intentions
abstract: Shows how sadness alters information processing, making people more cautious about sharing health claims but also more susceptible to risk-focused messaging.

title: Brain correlates of sadness in music: An exploratory ALE meta-analysis
abstract: Identifies consistent activation in emotional memory networks during music-induced sadness, revealing how aesthetic experiences engage ancient reward-emotion pathways.

title: Sadness regulation in daily life in remitted depression: Regulatory repertoire composition and affect-dependent effectiveness
abstract: Demonstrates how recovered individuals use diverse emotion regulation strategies flexibly to manage sadness, highlighting the importance of contextual adaptation.

title: Emotion Dynamic During Sad Events: The Relation Among Attachment Security, Loneliness and Sadness-Related Emotional Profiles
abstract: Reveals distinct patterns of sadness expression in children tied to attachment styles, showing how early relationships shape emotional development.

title: The Social Value of Sadness: A Pathway to Sympathy and Prosocial Behavior in Middle-Childhood
abstract: Documents sadness's adaptive role in fostering empathy and helping behaviors, challenging cultural biases against negative emotions.

title: Deconstructing 'Negative Emotions': A Paradigm Shift in Understanding Sadness
abstract: Proposes a cultural reevaluation of sadness as an essential adaptive emotion rather than a pathology to be eliminated.

title: Posterior cortical atrophy and logopenic variant primary progressive aphasia are more specific for Alzheimer's disease pathology than probable Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Research shows that atypical Alzheimer's presentations like posterior cortical atrophy (vision problems) and logopenic aphasia (language difficulties) may be more reliable indicators of Alzheimer's pathology than typical memory symptoms.

title: Provider and patient perspectives on the diagnosis and treatment of Alzheimer's disease: A global perspective from the Global Alzheimer's Leadership Series (GoALS)
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Global experts discuss the relationship between biological changes and clinical symptoms in Alzheimer's, highlighting the need for personalized approaches in diagnosis and treatment.

title: Considerations in Alzheimer's Disease in Women
abstract: Examines why women are disproportionately affected by Alzheimer's, exploring hormonal factors, biomarker differences, and implications for diagnosis and treatment.

title: Analyzing the 'bradykinesia complex' in GBA1-associated Parkinson's disease: A series of three cases
abstract: This study examined movement patterns in Parkinson's patients with genetic variants, finding that different genetic backgrounds lead to distinct types of movement impairment and responses to medication.

title: Non-pharmacological interventions for anxiety and depression in Parkinson's disease
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
abstract: This review protocol examines how non-drug treatments like therapy and exercise might help manage the emotional symptoms that often accompany Parkinson's disease.

title: Psychomotor retardation and risk of Parkinson's disease in unipolar depression: A retrospective cohort study
abstract: Research found that people with depression who experience slowed movement (psychomotor retardation) may have a higher risk of developing Parkinson's later in life.

title: Mapping public knowledge of Parkinson's disease in Portugal: a cross-sectional survey of knowledge, perceptions and attitudes
abstract: A survey revealed gaps in public understanding about Parkinson's symptoms and treatments, highlighting the need for better education about this growing neurological condition.

title: Better Conversations With Parkinson's: Feasibility and Acceptability of a Novel Communication Partner Training Telehealth Intervention
journal: International journal of language & communication disorders
abstract: A training program helped caregivers communicate more effectively with Parkinson's patients, addressing the speech and facial expression difficulties common in the disease.

title: Biofeedback in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review with meta-analysis
abstract: Biofeedback techniques that provide real-time information about movement helped Parkinson's patients improve their walking and balance more than standard therapy alone.
